architecture.mechanism: Gain-scheduling-based Energy Management System using a rule-based approach to split power between hybrid energy storage devices (battery and supercapacitor) according to operating mode.
architecture.intervention: Apply a gain-scheduling, rule-based Energy Management System to the electric vehicle propulsion motor that dynamically splits propulsive power demand between a high-energy battery pack and a high-power supercapacitor module, selecting power-split gains based on the driving mode (e.g., cruise vs. transient acceleration/braking regen) rather than using a single fixed battery-only source.
architecture.expected_effect: Improved overall energy conversion efficiency of the EV propulsion motor drivetrain by offloading transient/high-power peaks and regenerative events to the supercapacitor (reducing battery I²R losses and charge/discharge inefficiencies) while the battery supplies steady baseline power, yielding lower energy losses per mile than a battery-only Tesla-class configuration.
architecture.falsification_test: Run a standardized drive cycle (e.g., UDDS or US06) on a dynamometer with a conventional battery-only EV powertrain versus the same motor coupled to the gain-scheduled battery+supercapacitor EMS; record kWh consumed per mile and motor/controller losses via power analyzer at the DC bus and inverter output. The mechanism is supported if the hybrid EMS powertrain shows a statistically significant reduction (>3%, p<0.05) in kWh/mile and measured conversion losses versus the battery-only baseline; otherwise the mechanism is falsified.
